title: L26/O-202 Repurposing aminophylline to improve pregnancy outcomes in POSEIDON group 4 patients undergoing assisted reproductive technology: evidence from a cohort study and follicular microenvironment profiling
abstract: Can oral aminophylline enhance oocyte competence and clinical outcomes in advanced-age women with diminished ovarian reserve (POSEIDON Group 4)? Oral aminophylline pre-treatment significantly increases live birth rate in POSEIDON Group 4 women by optimizing the follicular microenvironment and enhancing mitochondrial function. Management of POSEIDON Group 4 patients remains a challenge in ART due to age-related oocyte senescence and metabolic insufficiency. While various interventions, including hormonal treatments and follicle-stimulating agents, have been explored to improve pregnancy outcomes, the clinical impact of oral aminophylline, a phosphodiesterase inhibitor (PDEI), has not been well established. Previous studies have demonstrated that PDEIs can enhance intracellular cAMP levels and promote oocyte maturation in animal models. However, their application as a systemic metabolic rescuer to improve definitive pregnancy outcomes, particularly live birth rate in women with diminished ovarian reserve, has not been conclusively proven. This single-center, translational cohort study was conducted from December 2022 to December 2024. The clinical cohort included 1,718 POSEIDON Group 4 patients (Aminophylline(AP) group, n = 140; Control group, n = 1,578). A mechanistic arm was also incorporated, utilizing multi-omic profiling of follicular fluid (FF) and cumulus granulosa cells (CGCs) from a representative subset. The study focused on assessing the effects of oral aminophylline pre-treatment on ART outcomes and understanding underlying molecular mechanisms through transcriptomic and proteomic analysis. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 1,718 IVF/ICSI patients (140 in the AP group and 1,578 controls). The AP group received oral aminophylline (100mg, TID) for at least one month before stimulation, continuing until oocyte retrieval. Clinical outcomes were compared using multivariable logistic regression and propensity score matching (PSM). To investigate mechanisms, transcriptomic (RNA-seq of CGCs) and proteomic (LC-MS/MS of FF) analyses were performed to identify metabolic and signaling alterations induced by aminophylline. After propensity score matching (PSM), the AP group demonstrated significantly higher biochemical pregnancy rate (35.56% vs. 26.25%, P = 0.037). Clinical pregnancy rate (26.67% vs. 19.33%, P = 0.069) and live birth rate (17.04% vs. 11.46%, P = 0.092) showed positive trends. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified aminophylline as an independent predictor for biochemical pregnancy (aOR = 1.70, P = 0.018), clinical pregnancy (aOR = 1.64, P = 0.040), and live birth (aOR = 1.88, P = 0.032). Transcriptomic analysis revealed 1,228 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with significant upregulation in mitochondrial function and metabolic pathways, particularly the PI3K-Akt signaling and GnRH signaling pathways. Proteomic analysis of follicular fluid identified 13 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs), including IGFBP3 and IGFALS, key regulators of follicular development. These findings suggest that aminophylline treatment enhances oocyte quality and embryo implantation potential.Future research should explore the molecular mechanisms by which aminophylline affects follicular development, embryo implantation, and oocyte quality, focusing on mitochondrial dynamics, ROS, and metabolic reprogramming. Expanding studies to other patient groups and conducting randomized controlled trials with larger cohorts and advanced molecular profiling will help determine aminophylline’s broader therapeutic potential in ART. This study has limitations, including its retrospective design, insufficient sample size for detecting subtle effects, and unclear correlation between mitochondrial changes and improved pregnancy outcomes. Further research is needed to explore the role of endometrial receptivity, immune modulation, and other factors in enhancing ART outcomes. This study marks the first clinical translation of Aminophylline as a “fertility-enhancing drug” for advanced-age patients.Aminophylline may improve pregnancy outcomes in POSEIDON group 4 patients by enhancing mitochondrial function and metabolic pathways. Future research should explore its mechanisms and broader applications to validate findings and optimize ART outcomes. No
authors: Y. Liu; Z. Chuan-chuan; W. Dan-dan; P. Jintao; W. Qiu-li; Z. Mei-jia; L. Xiaoyan

title: Oral LNAD+ rapidly elevates whole blood intracellular NAD and metabolic flux without elevating plasma NAD: evidence from a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Declines in nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) are linked to metabolic stress accompanying aging and disease. While precursor-based approaches elevate systemic NAD, their clinical translation can be constrained by biosynthetic bottlenecks and first-pass metabolism. RENEWAL-NAD+ (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07336836; retrospectively registered 01/04/2026) was a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 0/1b trial in healthy adults aged 45-75 years (60 randomized; primary analysis n = 50) evaluating 5 days of oral LathMized® NAD+ (LNAD+), a physicochemically modulated formulation that alters the supramolecular organization and solution behavior of NAD+ while preserving its native molecular structure. The primary endpoints were change in intracellular NAD (icNAD), measured in whole blood, and circulating NAD (cirNAD), measured in separated plasma, relative to baseline. LNAD+ produced a rapid and pronounced increase in icNAD, with a 53% elevation versus placebo at Day 6 (p = 5.48e-14; Hedges' g = 3.66), while cirNAD was unchanged (p = 0.60), demonstrating compartment-selective augmentation. Plasma NAD catabolites increased substantially (1-methyl-nicotinamide, MeNAM p = 5.39e-13; N1-methyl-2-pyridone-5-carboxamide, 2PY p = 2.95e-16), consistent with downstream engagement of NAD metabolic flux. Exploratory analyses identified non-overlapping correlates for the two compartments (cirNAD tracking inflammatory and metabolic markers, icNAD tracking red blood cell indices and NAM). Treatment was very well tolerated: symptom incidence was comparable between groups (p = 0.68), only one mild adverse event (nausea, Grade 1) occurred in the LNAD+ arm, and no secondary clinical, vital-sign, wellbeing, or wearable-derived endpoint survived multiplicity correction. These data demonstrate rapid intracellular NAD augmentation after oral LNAD+ dosing with pharmacodynamic evidence of downstream metabolism, compartment-specific physiological signatures, and a favorable short-term safety profile, with exploratory multi-omic analyses ongoing.
authors: S. Kornilov; W. Hastings; L. McGrath; Michael Leitz-Langan; A. Magis; Steve M. Coppess; Wendy Komac
